clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old woman presented to the ED with abdominal pain radiating to her back and chest, rectal tenesmus, gas pains, and abdominal distention. Initial assessment revealed diffuse abdominal tenderness, elevated blood pressure (170/68), and no pulse discrepancies. A CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis with contrast was ordered, which revealed a Stanford Type A aortic dissection extending from the aortic root to the aortic bifurcation. She was medically managed with nicardipine and esmolol infusions, underwent emergent cardiothoracic surgical intervention, made a complete recovery, and was discharged after 8 days.
